title: Joshua Morizono beats Ma Lin in a deciding game to become world para champion as Aaron McKibbin takes silver
seo_title: Joshua Morizono wins World Para Championships class 9 gold
description: Joshua Morizono beat Australia's Ma Lin 3-2 for the class 9 world title in Pattaya, while Aaron McKibbin lost the class 8 final to Russia's Artem Iakovlev.
standfirst: The Welshman, who lives in Japan, took the decider 11-9 against the man who beat him at the last two Paralympics, on the final day of the World Para Championships in Thailand.
body: Joshua Morizono is a world champion. The Welshman beat Australia's Ma Lin 3-2 in the men's class 9 singles final at the World Para Championships in Pattaya on Thursday, taking the deciding game 11-9 against the player who had beaten him at the Tokyo and Paris Paralympics.

Aaron McKibbin could not make it two British titles on the final day. The 34-year-old lost the class 8 final 3-1 to Russia's Artem Iakovlev, the world No 10, and takes silver, the first major singles final of his career ending a week that began with him in bed with illness.

Ma, the Chinese-born Australian who is one of the great names of para table tennis, led 8-4 in the first game. Morizono fought back to 9-9 before a forehand into the net gave Ma game point, and Ma took it 11-9.

Morizono won the second 11-7 and led the third 10-7, only to miss three forehands as Ma levelled at 10-10. He held his nerve to take it 12-10, but Ma won the fourth 11-4 and led 6-3 in the decider. Morizono pulled level at 8-8, and from 9-9 Ma put a forehand into the net. On match point Morizono served long, and Ma's receive went off the end.

"I think in the fifth I was always chasing," Morizono said afterwards. He described the long serve at 10-9 as a risk, guessing that Ma would try to flick it, and said he had expected Ma to find the edges at 9-9.
"For whatever reason there wasn't a moment in that match when my mind went to, 'I could be world champion'," he added. "It hasn't remotely sunk in yet that I'm world champion."

Morizono said he and his British Para Table Tennis coach, David McBeath, had watched a video of an earlier defeat by Ma the night before the final. The backhand, he said, had been the weak side of his game since he started playing, and "the fact that I was able to play with it freely was a game changer."

He also thanked his wife Misa, who watched in Pattaya with their four-month-old son, and Daisuke Ishida, who has worked with him for the past four months. "I feel like I'm the luckiest person on the planet to have found someone who supports me in the way she does," he said of Misa, who fed him multiball while pregnant.

The title follows Morizono's Commonwealth gold in Birmingham in 2022, when he also beat Ma in five games in the final, playing for Wales. On the way to this one he beat the American Tahl Leibovitz 3-2, Ukraine's Lev Kats 3-1 and France's Lucas Didier 3-0, hours after Didier had ended Laurens Devos's 11-year unbeaten run, as Eleven [reported on Wednesday](/news/world-para-championships-2026-mckibbin-morizono-finals-davies-bronze.html).

McKibbin and Morizono had pulled out of the men's doubles because McKibbin was ill, and he was not sure he would be fit for the singles. He beat Israel's Yehonatan Levi, Ukraine's Maksym Nikolenko and Italy's 17-year-old Ludovico Bini to reach the final.

Iakovlev won the first game 11-7 with serves that McKibbin said carried far more spin than he had expected. McKibbin levelled 11-8, but Iakovlev took the third 11-8 and pulled away 11-5 in the fourth.

"It was a tricky game," McKibbin said. "I don't think I played that bad, I think I played quite well." He felt the third game could have gone his way, said Iakovlev produced something special in the fourth, and added: "I've been playing some of the best table tennis of my career."

The Londoner said his previous two major championships had gone badly and that the silver would give him confidence for the next European Championships and for the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics, where he wants to go one step further.

Morizono and McKibbin's medals add to bronzes in Pattaya for Rob Davies in men's class 1 singles, Chris Ryan and Tom Matthews in men's class 4 doubles, and Will Bayley and Bly Twomey in mixed class 14 doubles.
